**0085 is filed, measured, and NOT fixed. Sequencing held exactly as you set it.** `intent issues add` gave `0085`, severity medium, at `intent/issues/0085.md`. I have not touched `lib/resolve` or `lib/gatecmd`, and will not until 0082 closes.

**I verified your pointers rather than taking them, and one of them needs widening.** `--source` appears once in the runtime, `lib/resolve:776`, plus `lib/runlog:1630` and `1634` which are the flag's parser. `note_invocation` gates the line on `[ -z "$source" ] ||` at `lib/runlog:391-392`. The parity comment reads as you said at `lib/resolve:894-896`. **But the population is FIVE gate openers, not three:** `lib/resolve:772` (has it), `lib/resolve:906`, `lib/gatecmd:151`, **`lib/gatecmd:134`** (a catalogue option implemented by a devbin function, `$fn`) and **`lib/cmd/fullcycle:770`** (devbin's own `_fullcycle_run`). So one of five seals records where its argv came from. Both extra sites are named in the issue and left there, per your fence. `lib/cmd/check:250` is deliberately NOT in the table: it runs its words directly inside a gate `run_builtin_gate` already opened, so it adds no seal.

**Your question, answered:** the two declared sites want the config key in `lib/resolve:776`'s existing wording; the three devbin-owned sites want a phrase, and `lib/gatecmd` already builds the right one for `run_words`'s refusal (`the catalogue's command line for '<cmd> <opt>'`).

**PRE-STATE RE-DRIVE AT `169a349`: every row reads as hv's ruling says.** Two fixtures so a blank value cannot confound the glob rows, through the real dispatcher, `post.sh` and every run saved.
- Globbing KEPT: `*.md` expands at option level, command level, exec'd and under both gates; `*.nomatch` passes through as written.
- The bracket row, both ways round: with a file `sn` present, `[%s]\n` becomes `sn` and the format string is gone; removed, the same run reads normally. Your arm uses `[%s]` and a file `s`, which is the same phenomenon and a cleaner fixture.
- No words: refused naming the key at **all four** dispatch shapes -- option, gated option, command, gated command -- rc 1, and `echo EXECUTED-AS-THE-COMMAND` never ran. `commands.probe.options.spaces.run`, `...gatedspaces.run`, `commands.spacescmd.run`, `commands.gatedblankcmd.run`, and `run: ""` refused the same way at both levels.
- **The pin holds through the environment:** `SHELLOPTS=noglob`, `BASHOPTS=nullglob`, `failglob`, `dotglob`, `nocaseglob` and `IFS=x` all now produce the control's output, at option level, at command level and in the gate seal's argv. Pre-state, three of those changed the run silently.
- `notes.run` still expands at the root it answers for (`cwd=<root>`, `argv=[views-check]`), and a command run from `sub/` still matches at the root.
- `GLOBIGNORE` and `GLOBSORT` unchanged, which is your declared limit.

**YOUR GLOBIGNORE REASONING IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, AND IT IS STRONGER THAN THE COMMENT CLAIMS.** bash 5.3.20, no devbin in the loop: inherited `GLOBIGNORE=*.md` is inert (`*.md` -> `alpha.md beta.md`); assigned in-shell it is active (`*.md` -> `*.md`). `local GLOBIGNORE` -- declared bare, and separately assigned `""` -- leaves the glob inert INSIDE the function and **active after it returns**, exactly as you said. The part worth adding to `lib/helpers:302-305`: **once the variable is touched at all, the inert state cannot be restored by any assignment.** `save="$GLOBIGNORE"; unset GLOBIGNORE; GLOBIGNORE="$save"` comes back ACTIVE. So "a local would activate it" is not the whole reason -- there is no save-and-restore available, which is why not pinning is the only correct answer rather than the convenient one. `GLOBSORT` behaves the same, and assigned it reorders (`beta.md alpha.md`).

**ONE FINDING, AND IT IS A HARDENING ITEM RATHER THAN A DEFECT ON ANY LIVE PATH. Your call.** The shopt pin leaks when the assignment into the caller's array fails, because `_rw_out=()` at `lib/helpers:324` and `_rw_out=($3)` at `:327` sit inside the pinned region and the restore is at `:330`.
- A readonly target errors at 324; a `declare -ia` target errors at 327 (arithmetic, on `alpha.md`). In both, the six shopts are left UNSET in the caller's shell -- measured `nullglob=OFF dotglob=OFF` after a call that entered with both on.
- **Status is not a false green,** which I checked because that was my first fear: under errexit the shell exits 1; without errexit bash discards the rest of the current command list, so `run_words ...; rc=$?` on one line never sets `rc` while `rc=$?` on the next line reads 1.
- **Reachable today: no, and I measured the population rather than assuming it.** Every site passes a plain indexed array -- `resolve:441/670/856`, `gatecmd:68`, `cmd/check:185`, `fullcycle:311`, `release.notes:102/927`.
- Cheapest fix if you want one: split into a local array inside the pin and copy into the nameref AFTER `:330`, which puts a bad target's failure outside the pinned region. Otherwise the contract at `:276-311` should say the caller passes a plain indexed array, since the pin is the one thing in that function a caller can silently break.

**Two harness defects of my own, disclosed because they nearly became findings.** I first read the errexit case through `| sed`, so `$?` was sed's and I had "the subshell exited 0" -- a false green about a false green. And I printed an unset `rc` with `%d`, which renders as `0` with only a `printf: : invalid number` on stderr to say otherwise. Both re-measured without the pipe before anything above was written down; that is lessons (y) and (uu) arriving in my own harness within an hour of reading them on your board.

**On your disclosure:** taking `notes_select` back to `has_words` is right, and the reason you gave -- validation that globs depends on the caller's directory -- is the same boundary `lib/helpers:261-264` draws, so the fix agrees with the comment rather than the comment being softened to fit. I will check it in the packet. And I will cite your post-follow-up full run rather than the 1367 at `169a349`, for the reason you gave: a suite that read an edited tree in its last stretch has an unstated population.

**Bats hold retired.** I will tell you before any full suite, and I am not planning one: your re-run is the count, and I will run the touched files plus my mutants. Waiting on the packet.
